summary: Every offline command that can emit caveats (offlineIDCmd, shared by offline_performance/offline_classes_show/offline_classes_structure/offline_strength; newOfflineIntervalsCmd; newOfflineWorkoutCmd, which builds its own RunE independently) must merge caveats into the response's existing top-level map via printOfflineWithCaveats, never nest the payload under a fresh "result" key. A field's location in the response must never depend on whether that particular call happened to produce a caveat -- any new offline command with its own caveat-bearing RunE must route through printOfflineWithCaveats too, not reinvent the wrap-on-caveat pattern.
reason: A seventh live post-fix verification sweep found offlineIDCmd nested its whole payload under "result" only when a caveat fired, so the correct --select path was data-dependent and unknowable in advance -- an agent had to make an unprojected call first just to discover which shape it got back. Fixing offlineIDCmd and newOfflineIntervalsCmd surfaced that newOfflineWorkoutCmd had the identical hand-rolled wrap-in-"result" logic (it predates printOfflineWithCaveats and was never migrated), so it was fixed in the same pass to keep the contract uniform across every offline command.
validated_outcome: go build/vet/test/govulncheck and verify_skill.py all green. TestOfflineIDCmdKeepsFieldsAtTopLevelRegardlessOfCaveat covers both offlineIDCmd (via offline_performance w2, which has no performance record) and offline_workout (via a seeded workout_details-only record), asserting no "result" key, real fields present at top level, caveats present, and --select working identically either way. Live-verified against the real account: offline_workout on a real workout lacking a workouts record returns detail and caveats both at top level with no result wrapper, and --select caveats returns exactly the caveats array.
